data.body:
## RCA — confirmed by observing the guard fire (not by reading source)

**Observation.** Drove the real `_no_repo_commits` fixture in a disposable worktree by having a
test run `git commit --allow-empty` against the checkout, and captured what it printed verbatim:

```
Failed: Test moved the repo HEAD (cc3fba5cfb -> 018dbb1462): it committed into the rebar
checkout instead of an isolated tmp tracker. Isolate the git writes - pin
GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES to the tmp root (see tests/scripts/graph/conftest.py::
_isolate_git_from_enclosing_repo) or init the tracker as its own git repo. Undo the stray
commit(s) with: git reset --hard cc3fba5cfb
```

(Reported as an ERROR at teardown, alongside the test's own `passed` - `1 passed, 1 error`.)

**Mechanism.** The fixture's only evidence is two `git rev-parse HEAD` samples taken around the
test body (`tests/conftest.py:635,639`). A sha inequality across a wall-clock window carries no
attribution signal whatsoever: a commit made by the test's own subprocess and a commit made by
another session sharing the checkout are the same kind of git object, by the same user, in the
same repo. The guard nonetheless emits two unearned claims - the causal one ("it committed into
the rebar checkout") and the remedial one (`git reset --hard <before>`, stated unconditionally).
Followed literally by a reader whose HEAD moved externally, that reset discards another
process's commit *and* every uncommitted change in the worktree.

This is the same shape as the leak guard, and identical reasoning: `746c-185a-0e48-4b83` /
Gerrit 1978 concluded "no attribution signal is available to a snapshot diff". Nothing cheaper
is available here either, so the remedy must be conditioned rather than made smarter.

**The external cause is real and already documented.** `docs/local-dev-env.md:434-442` lists
`_no_repo_commits` among the guards that a "concurrent commit, rebase, branch switch, or stray
file" fires on, attributing it to "an arbitrary, innocent" test. The message therefore
contradicts the project's own documented account of when this guard fires. Two independent
session records in `tests/fixtures/dc_wiki_corpus/` describe exactly this misfire ("an artifact
of my own concurrent `git commit`, not a test defect"; "running a rebase during a background
pytest produced 8 spurious failures + 33 errors").

**Legitimacy: `defect`.** Cited authority: `docs/local-dev-env.md:434-442` (above), plus the
invariant established for the sibling guard in `tests/_isolation.py::leak_failure_message` and
pinned by `tests/unit/test_external_mutation_diagnostics.py` - a shared-checkout diagnostic must
not assert the cause it cannot know. Detection is correct and stays exactly as-is; only the
message is wrong.

**Defect origin: `4c79-3873-807d-4a0d` (gusto-pixel-signal), by scope-of-work.**
`git blame -w -C -M -L 640,648 -- tests/conftest.py` puts every implicated line on
`d8b077451be` (2026-06-11), the commit that introduced the guard together with this message;
`b42d68c2d21` touched only line 645 (a file-path reference) and is a carrier, not the origin.
Date test: the lines date to the guard's own inception and there is no good->bad transition -
this is an **omission**, not a regression, so attribution is to the ticket whose scope was
"write the guard and its diagnostic". That commit carries no `rebar-ticket:` trailer (it
predates the convention) but names `(4c79-3873)` in its subject, which resolves to the task
"Repo-isolation guard: fail tests that commit to / dirty the checkout" - whose acceptance
criteria cover the guard's failure behaviour, so a reviewer there could plausibly have caught
it. Close class: `plan_defect` (the originating plan scoped detection only, never remedy safety).
